The Boeing OREIO design aims to reduce fuel burn and noise while meeting NASA's Environmentally Responsible Aviation (ERA) project goals.
The OREIO design uses open rotor engines.
The wingspan constraint for the OREIO design is 65m (213.25ft).
The objective function for design optimization in the OREIO study is fuel consumption.
The FLOPS software is a multidisciplinary system of computer programs for conceptual and preliminary design and evaluation of advanced aircraft concepts.
The FLOPS weight routines assume a home plate shape for the cabin.
The regression equation used to estimate the centerbody weight in FLOPS is W = K *0.316(TOGW)0.167(S)1.061 cabin s cabin.
The Boeing and FLOPS estimates for gross weight and empty weight are within 1% and 2% respectively.
The OREIO primary structure is analyzed using finite element method (FEM) using Nastran.
The PRSEUS concept is used for highly-integrated stitched-composite airframe structures tailored and optimized to exploit the orthotropic nature and processing advantages of carbon fiber materials.
The main challenge in modeling stiffened panels in a conceptual design environment is significant challenges in terms of FEM model size and complexity.

The goal of the Environmentally Responsible Aviation (ERA) project is to reduce noise (42db cumulative below the Stage 4 certification level), fuel burn (50% reduction compared to currently operating aircraft), and emissions (75% reduction in nitrogen oxide compared to the current standard).
The cruise Mach number for the OREIO design is 0.8.
The maximum sink rate at landing for the OREIO design is 8ft/sec.
The VSP model is used to generate geometry data for the structural analysis.
The Boeing and FLOPS weight estimates have some differences in sub-component outputs.
